// Regression fixture, added alongside a PopNesting fix found while
// building the Java port (counter.go): a function whose body defines a
// local class with an inline method does NOT score that method
// separately at all for plain C/C++ -- base CLikeStates' `_state_imp` is
// fully opaque (clike.go's stateImp), so nothing inside an already-open
// function body is ever re-dispatched through the declaration-parsing
// chain that would confirm "method" as its own function; its conditions
// simply fold into the ENCLOSING function, exactly like a lambda's do.
// Measured directly to confirm this (not assumed): only ONE function
// (outer) is reported, and its complexity includes the local class's
// method's own "if" too. This means the PopNesting fix itself (restoring
// ctx.current to an enclosing function still open on the nesting stack)
// is UNREACHABLE for plain C/C++ specifically -- there is no C++ shape
// that creates two NESTED function-tagged nesting entries in the first
// place, since only a real (non-opaque) function body can confirm a
// nested declaration, and C/C++'s is always opaque. Java's own port is
// where this fixture's sibling construct (an anonymous class's inline
// method) DOES create two nested function entries and DOES exercise the
// restore -- see java.go's package doc and its own corpus.
int outer(int n) {
    class Local {
    public:
        int method(int x) {
            if (x > 0) {
                return 1;
            }
            return 0;
        }
    };
    Local l;
    if (n > 0 && l.method(n) > 0) {
        return 1;
    }
    return 0;
}
